(2) The Python test oracle _dao_structure (python/tests/test_vectors.py:2356-2402) also does not check the flags byte; adding the vector with expected envelope_valid=False makes test_dao_origin_signature_vector fail its structurally_valid assertion — the oracle itself needs the one-line extension (option_type == 5 and (length != 18 or data[0] != 0) -> bad_option_length-or-new-reason). (3) dao_origin.py:296-298 already rejects data[0] != 0 as MALFORMED_OPTIONS at the structural stage, so the impl-side reason string to pin is the existing malformed_dao vocabulary with decision_stage=structural, envelope_valid=false, signature_valid=true (sign the nonzero-flags DAO itself; structural precedes crypto). (4) Vector construction: generator target() helper hardcodes flags=0 (generate_dao_origin_signature.py:61-62) — inline bytes([5, 18, flags, prefix_len]) + address with flags=0x01, then rejected('reject_target_flags_nonzero', 'd1', dao(...), 42, reason='malformed_dao', stage='structural'). (5) Consumer updates in the same landing: lichen-rpl/tests/dao_origin_vectors.rs malformed_dao arm asserts envelope.is_err() (message.rs envelope must add the body[0] != 0 reject to is_generalized_target_body or the envelope loop); lichen-node/tests/dao_origin_vectors.rs expected_outcome('malformed_dao') already maps to structural reject (node code fix is 3.1's extract_updates+envelope scope).
